explain: _tē_ is the accusative of _tū_: you as the thing seen. The verb ending _-ō_ already says “I”.
distractors: _tū_ is nominative: “you” as the one doing. As the thing seen, use _tē_.
_tibi_ is dative (“to you”). The thing seen is accusative: _tē_.
_tuī_ is genitive (“of you”). The thing seen is accusative: _tē_.

explain: _mē_ is the accusative of _ego_: me as the thing seen. _vidēs_ already says “you”.
distractors: _ego_ is nominative: “I” as the one doing. As the thing seen: _mē_.
_mihi_ is dative (“to me”). The thing seen is accusative: _mē_.
_meī_ is genitive (“of me”). The thing seen is accusative: _mē_.

explain: _mihi_ is the dative of _ego_: “to me” (the one who receives). _pānem_ is what is given.
distractors: _mē_ is accusative (“me” as the thing given). The person who receives is dative: _mihi_.
_ego_ is nominative (“I do it”). The one who receives is dative: _mihi_.
_meī_ is genitive (“of me”). The one who receives is dative: _mihi_.
_tē_ is accusative. The one who receives is dative: _tibi_.
_tū_ is nominative. The one who receives is dative: _tibi_.
_tuī_ is genitive (“of you”). The one who receives is dative: _tibi_.

explain: _nōs_ is both “we” and “us”: its nominative and accusative look the same. Here it is the thing seen. _vident_ says “they”.
distractors: _nōbīs_ is dative or ablative (“to us”). The thing seen is accusative: _nōs_.
_nostrī_ is genitive (“of us”). The thing seen is accusative: _nōs_.
_nōs_ is accusative. The ones who receive are dative: _nōbīs_.
_nostrī_ is genitive (“of us”). The ones who receive are dative: _nōbīs_.

explain: _vōs_ is both “you all” (nominative) and “you all” (accusative). Here it is the thing seen.
distractors: _vōbīs_ is dative or ablative (“to you all”). The thing seen is accusative: _vōs_.
_vestrī_ is genitive (“of you all”). The thing seen is accusative: _vōs_.

explain: _vōbīs_ is the dative of _vōs_: “to you all”.
distractors: _vōs_ is accusative. The ones who receive are dative: _vōbīs_.
_vestrī_ is genitive. The ones who receive are dative: _vōbīs_.
_tibi_ is “to you” (one person). For several people: _vōbīs_.

explain: With a personal pronoun, _cum_ is joined on to the end: _tēcum_ is “with you”. (Not _cum tē_.)
distractors: With a pronoun, _cum_ is attached to the end: _tēcum_.
